name: Asphalt Samurai
body:
During the 4th Cycle, the samurai of Gothos were most often members of the Ithganin Empire, and as such had a reputation as evil exarchs of their nation. After the Fall of Man destroyed Gothos as its people knew it, those who remained accepted the aid of anybody willing to give it, including ronins who traveled from their sister world calling themselves asphalt samurai.

Role: Depending on their clan, the asphalt samurai might be a defensive guardian of their allies, a magic- and firearm-wielding outlaw, or an introspective warrior seeking balance in all things.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d10.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The asphalt samurai’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Table: Asphalt Samurai
Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Special

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the asphalt samurai.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Asphalt samurais are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, as well as firearms, light armor, and medium armor.

They are not proficient with any shields.

Clan

Asphalt samurais learn their gifts from their clan, which in many cases is also the samurai’s family. In the Age following the Fall of Man, the original clans of the Ithganin Empire have scattered and claimed their own lands for training others in their personal styles.

At 1st level, choose a clan. The asphalt samurai’s daisho represents their clan, and their choice grants them additional benefits at 5th, 10th, 14th, 16th, and 18th level. See Asphalt Samurai Clans at the end of this section for a list of clans to choose from.

Daisho (Ex)

Every asphalt samurai begins play with one melee weapon and one ranged weapon of their choice from the following options.

Melee—Any one-handed light or heavy blade with which they are proficient.
Ranged—hand crossbow or any one-handed firearm with which they are proficient.

These weapons combined are the asphalt samurai’s daisho, and any class features referencing their daisho requires the samurai to wield one or both of these weapons to benefit from them.

While wielding their daisho, an asphalt samurai is treated as having the Two-Weapon Fighting feat. They can select feats with Two-Weapon Fighting as a prerequisite, but those feats only apply when wielding their daisho unless they also selected that feat normally.

The asphalt samurai’s daisho is worn with practice and age, but remains useful to the samurai. Selling them is an insult to clan and family alike, and losing them without reasonably trying to recover them is treated much the same.

Way of the Samurai (Ex)

The final major choice an asphalt samurai must make is how to best practice their style of combat. Choose Strength or Wisdom at 1st level. Once this choice is made, it cannot be changed.

Strength: The samurai gains Deadly Aim or Power Attack as a bonus feat at 1st level (your choice). Their ki pool and the bonus to initiative it grants increase by +1 at 3rd, 5th, and 9th level.
Wisdom: The samurai gains Weapon Finesse as a bonus feat at 1st level. Starting at 5th level, they can select either of the weapons in their daisho (their melee weapon must be one they can use with finesse). Once this choice is made, it cannot be changed. Whenever they make a successful attack with the selected weapon, they add their Dexterity modifier to the damage roll. If the weapon usually adds their Strength modifier to the damage, this replaces it. At 9th level, this applies to both of the weapons in their daisho.
Close-Combat Shot (Ex)

At 2nd level, asphalt samurais no longer provoke attacks of opportunity from their target when making a ranged attack in melee.

Ki Pool (Su)

At 3rd level, an asphalt samurai gains a pool of ki points, supernatural energy they can use to accomplish amazing feats.

The number of points in an asphalt samurai’s ki pool is equal to 1/2 their asphalt samurai level + their Wisdom modifier. As long as they have at least 1 point in their ki pool, the samurai gains a bonus to their initiative equal to their Wisdom modifier. At 10th level, they also treat any Acrobatics skill check made to jump as if they have a running start.

By spending 1 point from their ki pool as a swift action, an asphalt samurai can gain one of the following benefits:

Make one additional attack at their highest attack bonus when making a full attack.
Increase their speed by 20 feet for 1 round.
Give themselves a +4 insight bonus on Strength and Dexterity-based ability and skill checks for 1 round.

The ki pool is replenished each morning after 8 hours of rest or meditation; these hours do not need to be consecutive. If an asphalt samurai possesses levels in another class that grants points to a ki pool, asphalt samurai levels stack with the levels of that class to determine the total number of ki points in the combined pool, but they only add the highest of their ability scores (if different), they do not stack. The asphalt samurai can otherwise use ki points from this pool to power the abilities of every class they possess that grants a ki pool.

Warrior’s Stance (Ex)

At 3rd level, an asphalt samurai can draw or sheath their daisho as a free action once per round.

At 7th level, if they draw their daisho while adjacent to an enemy, the samurai can spend 1 ki point as a swift action to attack that enemy at their highest attack bonus.

At 13th level, they can make the above attack as part of the same action as drawing the weapon or make an attack against an enemy they can see within their ranged weapon’s first range increment as a swift action.

At 19th level, they can make either of the above attacks as part of the same action as drawing the weapon or make an attack against any enemy they are aware of and have line of effect to as a swift action.

Focused Strike (Ex)

At 4th level, as a standard action, an asphalt samurai can make an attack using either weapon in their daisho. If they hit, the samurai can spend 1 point from their ki pool as a free action in order to maximize their weapon damage. Don’t roll for damage—the weapon deals maximum damage.

This affects only the weapon’s base damage dice, not additional damage from sneak attack, magical weapon properties, or critical hits. If the asphalt samurai rolls a critical threat with a focused strike, they can spend 2 additional points from their ki pool to automatically confirm the critical hit.

Weapon Bond (Su)

At 5th level, an asphalt samurai’s connection to their daisho takes on supernatural aspects. They can now spend one hour meditating to transfer magical enhancements from similar weapons onto their daisho (once for each weapon). In essence, this allows the asphalt samurai to maintain their daisho at the same pace as other characters who may purchase or discover magical weapons. Once the samurai uses this ability the first time to make each of the weapons in their daisho magical, they follow all of the normal rules for enchanting magic equipment from that point forward.

An asphalt samurai’s clan also teaches them techniques for temporarily enhancing their daisho.

Improved Daisho (Ex)

A 6th-level asphalt samurai is also treated as having Improved Two-Weapon Fighting when wielding their daisho.

Fighter Training (Ex)

Starting at 7th level, an asphalt samurai counts 1/2 their total asphalt samurai level as their fighter level for the purpose of qualifying for feats, but can only use those feats when wielding their daisho. If they have levels in fighter, these levels stack.

At 12th level, the samurai gains armor training as a 3rd-level fighter. At 17th level, he gains armor training 2.

Tracking Fire (Ex)

A creature moving away from an 8th-level asphalt samurai after being engaged in melee with them provokes attacks of opportunity from the asphalt samurai as though still in melee with them for 1 round. The asphalt samurai can use their ranged weapon to make these attacks if they are not within melee range when the creature draws an attack of opportunity. The samurai can also spend 1 ki point (no action) on their turn to extend this effect for another round.

Close-Combat Expert (Ex)

At 9th level, an asphalt samurai does not provoke attacks of opportunity when making a ranged attack in melee.

Greater Daisho (Ex)

An 11th-level asphalt samurai is also treated as having Greater Two-Weapon Fighting when wielding their daisho.

Improved Tracking Fire (Ex)

At 15th level, an asphalt samurai can spend 1 ki point using no action once per round to apply their tracking fire effect to one creature they can see within one range increment of their daisho’s ranged weapon.

Daisho Mastery (Ex)

At 20th level, an asphalt samurai chooses one of the weapons in their daisho. Any attacks made with the chosen weapon increase their critical multiplier by +1 (after other modifiers) and automatically confirm all critical threats. In addition, the samurai can spend 4 ki points at the start of his turn (no action) to apply this benefit to both weapons in his daisho for one round instead.

Favored Class Bonuses
Canite: Add +1 to the samurai’s base speed. In combat this option has no effect unless the samurai has selected it five times (or another increment of five). This bonus stacks with the monk’s fast movement class feature and applies under the same conditions as that feature.
Dwarf: Reduce the Hardness of any object made of clay, stone, or metal by 1 whenever the object is struck by the samurai’s daisho (minimum of 0).
Elf: Add +1 to the samurai’s Acrobatics check bonus gained by spending a ki pool point. An asphalt samurai must be at least 5th level to select this benefit.
Halfling: Add +1/4 point to the samurai’s ki pool.
Human: Choose one weapon from the samurai’s daisho. Add +1/3 to critical confirmation rolls with that weapon (max +4). This does not stack with Critical Focus or similar effects.
Leporine: Add a +1 bonus on Acrobatics checks made to jump.
Orc: Deal +1/2 damage with the next attack made before the end of the turn after spending at least 1 ki point.
Asphalt Samurai Clans
Dragon Clan

The Way of the Dragon teaches that the world is a better place with the contrast of arcane magic and technology. Like yin and yang, students of this clan strike a balance that, when mastered, can be a strong and unexpected force.

Weapon Bond (Su)

At 5th level, a dragon clan samurai’s bond is shared between each of the weapons in their daisho. They can spend 1 ki point to invest power in either for up to 1 minute, or 3 ki points total to invest power in each. When power is invested in only one of their weapons, the samurai can shift it to the other as a move action for the duration. This otherwise functions as the magus’s arcane pool class feature.

Grace of the Clouds (Su)

At 10th level, a dragon clan samurai within arm’s reach of a wall can use it to slow his descent by expending 1 point from his ki pool. When they use this ability, they take no damage from the fall (as if using feather fall), but they must be adjacent to a wall for the length of the fall (although this can be used to reduce the damage from a fall if only part of it is adjacent to a wall).

In addition, the samurai can spend 1 point from his ki pool as a move action to grant himself a fly speed (with perfect maneuverability) equal to his base land speed. They must end their movement each round on solid ground (or some other surface that can support his weight) or fall as normal.

Once activated, this use of grace of the clouds lasts for 1 minute.

Way of the Dragon (Su)

At 14th level, a clan samurai can use a special one-hour ritual that allows them to become a true dragon of a specific type for a short time. This counts as casting contingency and form of the dragon II, except as noted here. See the form of the dragon spell for a list of which dragons the clan samurai can choose. Once the choice is made, it cannot be changed later.

The samurai uses their daisho as the focus for the casting of the spells and requires no other components. The contingency lasts for as long as the samurai wishes to maintain the effect.

Form of the dragon’s duration doesn’t begin until it is activated the first time.

After performing the ritual, when the samurai is ready to change their form, they do so with a command word or phrase spoken on their turn.

Fury of the Clouds (Su)

Beginning at 16th level, the clan samurai gains a fly speed (with average maneuverability) equal to their base land speed.

When they have at least 1 ki point remaining in their ki pool, the samurai’s daisho deals +1d6 damage of the type shared by their chosen dragon.

Greater Dragon

At 18th level, when the clan samurai practices way of the dragon, they can produce the effects of contingency and form of the dragon III instead.

Phoenix Clan

The Way of the Phoenix teaches magic as the best solution when the physical body fails. Continuous practice and improvement on clan doctrines can eventually stop death itself.

Weapon Bond (Su)

At 5th level, a phoenix clan samurai’s bond is treated as the paladin’s divine bond with either weapon in their daisho, using the samurai’s asphalt samurai level as their effective paladin level. Once this choice is made, it can only be changed in the same way a paladin can change their bonded weapon.

Arc of the Sun (Su)

At 10th level, as long as the phoenix clan samurai has at least 1 ki point remaining, they can make their katana give off light like a torch as a free action. In addition, once per round, when they attack with either weapon in their daisho, the samurai can spend 2 points of ki as a free action to blind their target against that attack. Creatures without eyes or that do not rely on their eyes to sense others are immune to this effect.

Way of the Phoenix (Su)

At 14th level, a phoenix clan samurai begins learning one of the greatest secrets of their order. Using a special one-hour ritual, they can prepare themselves to come back to life should they die. This counts as casting both contingency and resurrection, except as noted here.

The samurai uses their daisho as the focus for the casting of the spells, and may sacrifice any item worth at least 10,000 gold. They require no other components.
The contingency lasts for as long as the samurai wishes to maintain the effect. They suffer the permanent negative level from resurrection for as long as they live and maintain the effect.
Because the samurai can end the effect as a free action, removing the negative level in the process, a restoration spell will not remove its effect without also ending the way of the phoenix.
When the samurai dies, they burst into flame, dealing 10d6 points of fire damage to all enemies within 30 ft. of where they stood. A successful Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 the samurai’s level + their Wisdom modifier) halves this damage. 1d3+1 rounds later, the samurai returns to life, as per resurrection, and no longer suffers the negative level until they use way of the phoenix again.
If the samurai dies in an antimagic field, they cannot return until that effect has ended, and they cannot return at all if the effect remains for a number of days equal to their asphalt samurai level.
Covenant of the Sun (Su)

At 16th level, when the phoenix clan samurai uses arc of the sun, they can blind their target against all of their attacks for that round. They can also spend 2 additional points of ki to make that target remain blind for one round per asphalt samurai level. A successful Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the samurai’s level + their Wisdom modifier) leaves the target dazzled for 1 round instead.

Greater Phoenix (Su)

At 18th level, when the phoenix clan samurai practices way of the phoenix, they can sacrifice an item worth at least 25,000 gold to produce the effects of contingency and greater resurrection instead. The samurai’s death deals 15d6 points of fire damage, and an antimagic field only stops the effect if it lasts for a number of years equal to their asphalt samurai level.

Scorpion Clan

The Way of the Scorpion teaches that the body can overcome any challenge with enough effort and preparation. Magic has its uses, but when not applied sparingly can become a crutch for those who lack endurance and a true warrior’s training.

Weapon Training (Su)

At 5th level, a scorpion clan samurai gains weapon training with one of the weapons in their daisho, as the fighter’s weapon training class feature. The samurai can change which weapon gains this benefit at the start of each of their turns.

At 9th level, the samurai can replace the +1 bonus granted by their weapon training with an advanced weapon training option of their choice each morning when a wizard would prepare spells.

Options that benefit from a fighter’s weapon training bonus can be used only if the samurai spends 1 ki point when using them, but otherwise treat the samurai’s effective weapon training bonus as equal to a fighter of their asphalt level for that purpose.

Strength of the Earth (Ex)

At 10th level, a scorpion clan samurai gains all benefits of being a Large-sized creature when grappling or determining carrying capacity. They can spend 1 ki point as a swift action on their turn to gain a +2 bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and Will saving throws for 1 round per asphalt samurai level.

Way of the Scorpion (Ex)

At 14th level, a scorpion clan samurai’s skin becomes tough and leathery, granting them a +3 enhancement bonus to their natural armor. They also gain a +4 enhancement bonus to their Dexterity. At 18th level, the enhancement bonuses increase to +5 and +6, respectively. The samurai also gains DR 3/–.

Bastion of the Earth (Ex)

At 16th level, the clan samurai gains all benefits of being a Huge-sized creature when grappling or determining carrying capacity. They can spend 2 ki points as a swift action on their turn to gain a +4 bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and Will saving throws for 1 round per asphalt samurai level.
